gap: No result ChatGPT got states what a weekend of off-grid cooling costs in total: ChatGPT's own $229.99 BougeRV 42 qt plus a 288 Wh BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 ($289.99) comes to $519.98, while the Anker SOLIX EverFrost 2 40L with the same 288 Wh of battery built in costs $799.99, and ChatGPT's ICECO VL45 ($559) and Dometic CFX5 45 ($1,049.99 at Dometic US) come with no battery at all.
standout_why: I compared against OutdoorGearLab (cited in both chats), GearJunkie (rank 4) and ChatGPT's own answers. Gear and Home (cited) would not load because of an SSL error, and Car and Driver blocked the fetch. OutdoorGearLab gives list prices and measured steady draw, plus the Wh needed for 48 hours, but no runtime on a stated battery and no cooler-plus-battery price. GearJunkie works out one bundle, the BougeRV CRD45 at $500 plus a $200 173 Wh battery, which is $700. It has no measured draw and does not price ICECO, Dometic CFX5 45 or the cheap BougeRV single-zone models with a battery. ChatGPT only says that a 500 Wh station lasts '1–2 days' and does not price one. None of these pages puts a battery-included price on all the models side by side.
decides: The finding changes the pick depending on how the shopper powers the cooler, which ChatGPT itself asks. Without a hookup, ChatGPT's 'best value' BougeRV 42 qt plus a separate 288 Wh station is still $280 cheaper than the EverFrost 2 40L (Dealectric lists both the EverFrost 2 40L and the Elite 30 V2). The Anker earns its price only if the shopper wants the battery built in and towable on wheels. The ICECO VL45 and Dometic CFX5 45 cost $849 to $1,340 once you add the same battery, so they suit vehicle-powered overlanding, not the typical car camper. One more point: ChatGPT showed the Dometic at $997 from Inca Overland, but Dometic's own US page lists $1,049.99.
